claim: Sri Lanka's Muslim communities should be understood as the product of layered Indian Ocean mobility rather than a single Arab founding population: early Arab- and Persian-speaking Muslim traders, later South Indian Muslim commercial networks, local marriage and settlement, and subsequent colonial classifications all contributed to communities later grouped under labels such as Ceylon Moor/Sri Lankan Moor.
bounded_by: The relative demographic weight of Arab/Persian, South Indian and local ancestry cannot be inferred from merchant narratives alone. Do not turn a cultural-commercial genealogy into a biological ancestry claim.
notes: Corrects the seed Wikipedia article's overly linear Arab-descendant framing while preserving the central role of Indian Ocean Muslim trade networks.
